record.original_question: Let P(z) be a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree d >= 2 written in the form P(z) = sum_{i=1}^k h alpha_i, z i^d with isotropic vectors alpha_i in C^n, and define the graph G(P) to have vertex set {1, 2, ..., k} with an edge between i and j exactly when <alpha_i, alpha_j> is nonzero. What necessary or sufficient conditions on this labeled graph G(P) ensure that P(z) is Hessian nilpotent?

evidence.quote: We fix a homogeneous harmonic polynomial P(z) in C[z] of degree d >= 2, and assume that P(z) is given by Eq. (8.2) for some alpha_i in X(C^n) (1 <= i <= k).
The set of vertices of G(P) will be the set of positive integers [k] := {1, 2, . . . , k}. The vertices i and j of G(P) are connected by an edge iff <alpha_i, alpha_j> != 0.
Open Problem 8.4. (a) Find some necessary or sufficient conditions on the (labeled) graph G(P) such that the homogeneous harmonic polynomial P(z) is HN.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n,d,k$ be positive integers with $d\geq 2$. Call a vector $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^n$ isotropic if $\langle\alpha,\alpha\rangle:=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i^2=0$, and write $X(\mathbb{C}^n)$ for the set of isotropic vectors. Consider a homogeneous polynomial $P(z)\in\mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ of degree $d$ of the special form
$$P(z)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\langle\alpha_i,z\rangle^{d},\qquad \alpha_i\in X(\mathbb{C}^n).$$
(Any such $P$ is automatically harmonic, i.e. $\Delta P=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\partial^2 P/\partial z_j^2=0$.) Say that $P$ is Hessian nilpotent (HN) if its Hessian matrix $\bigl(\partial^2 P/\partial z_i\partial z_j\bigr)_{1\le i,j\le n}$ is a nilpotent matrix of polynomial entries.

Associate to such a representation of $P$ the labeled graph $G(P)$ on vertex set $[k]=\{1,2,\dots,k\}$ in which vertices $i$ and $j$ ($i\neq j$) are joined by an edge if and only if $\langle\alpha_i,\alpha_j\rangle\neq 0$.

Problem: Find nontrivial necessary conditions, and find nontrivial sufficient conditions, on the labeled graph $G(P)$ that guarantee $P(z)$ is Hessian nilpotent.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the literature on Hessian nilpotent polynomials connected to the Jacobian conjecture. Subsequent works on HN polynomials and the vanishing conjecture (e.g., Zhao's papers in Annales Polonici Mathematici and J. Pure Appl. Algebra) continue to list characterizing HN polynomials of the form $\sum\langle\alpha_i,z\rangle^d$ via combinatorial/graph data as unresolved; partial results exist (e.g., for small $k$ or linearly independent $\alpha_i$), but no general necessary-and-sufficient graph-theoretic criterion is known.

status_evidence.title: Some properties of and open problems on Hessian nilpotent polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Several open problems have been proposed for further study on HN polynomials and their (deformed) inversion pairs.
status_evidence.claim: Graph-theoretic characterization of Hessian nilpotency for harmonic polynomials given as sums of d-th powers of isotropic linear forms is listed among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Two results on homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Partial results on homogeneous HN polynomials, including special cases involving isotropic vectors.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are available; a complete graph-theoretic criterion remains open.
